quiz.title: Unit 5 SAQ 02
quiz.headline: Industrialization and society
quiz.prompt: Answer all parts of the question.
quiz.instructions: Answer all three parts. For each part, Answer the question directly, Prove it with specific historical evidence, and Explain how the evidence supports your answer. On the AP exam each part earns one point. This is self-assessment practice, not official College Board scoring.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice in AP short-answer format. Model answers show one strong response; other accurate, well-supported answers can earn the point.

scaffold.label: Answer
scaffold.text: Respond directly to the task verb: identify, describe, or explain.

scaffold.label: Prove
scaffold.text: Name a specific person, place, institution, or development.

scaffold.label: Explain
scaffold.text: Show how or why the evidence answers the question.

parts.prompt: Identify ONE reason industrialization began in Great Britain in the late 1700s.
criteria: Connects the reason to industrial production.

model.answer: Britain had coal and iron ore near rivers and ports that factories and steam engines could use.
model.prove: Coalfields in northern England and Wales supplied fuel for steam engines and iron smelting, and coastal and river transport carried the materials to market.
model.explain: Cheap fuel and easy transport lowered the cost of making iron and textiles with machines, which made factory production profitable.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also identify agricultural improvements that pushed workers toward towns, capital from overseas trade, a stable government that protected property, or raw cotton and markets in the colonies.

parts.prompt: Describe ONE way industrialization changed family life or work for women or children in the 1800s.

model.answer: Many women and children worked outside the home for wages in factories and mines.
model.prove: In British textile mills and coal mines, children and women worked long hours, which prompted inquiries and laws such as the Factory Act of 1833 and the Mines Act of 1842.
model.explain: Work moved away from the household and into workplaces run by owners, which changed how families earned a living.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also describe the ideal of a middle-class home in which wives stayed at home, or the growth of domestic service as a major occupation for working-class women.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way governments or reformers responded to conditions in industrial cities by 1900.
criteria: Names a specific response, such as a law or movement.
Explains how it addressed a problem of industrial life.

model.answer: Governments passed public health laws to improve sanitation in crowded cities.
model.prove: After cholera epidemics, Britain's Public Health Act of 1848 and later laws led cities to build sewers and provide cleaner water.
model.explain: Rapid urban growth had produced crowded slums where disease spread, so public works for water and waste reduced death rates and showed a larger role for government.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also explain factory legislation, the legal recognition of trade unions, the extension of the vote to working men, or Bismarck's insurance programs in Germany.
